label: Cisco ISE

corePack.why: Authentication failures are the first signal that users cannot get on the network.
corePack.whyNow: A spike in 802.1X failures is an outage, not a report.

corePack.why: PSN TPS headroom tells you the pair will survive a node loss before it happens.
corePack.whyNow: Capacity is a leading indicator for identity outages.
corePack.metric: Authentications per second versus licensed/SLO headroom

corePack.why: Replication lag splits policy: some PSNs authorize yesterday's rules.
corePack.whyNow: Unsynced nodes create un-debuggable allow/deny disagreements.
corePack.metric: PSN sync lag and replication health codes 60100/60101

corePack.why: Expired admin, EAP, or pxGrid certificates take the whole NAC plane down.
corePack.whyNow: Certificate expiry is scheduled pain you can still prevent.
corePack.metric: Days to certificate expiry by role

corePack.why: Node CPU, memory, disk, and threads are the health of the identity control plane.
corePack.whyNow: A saturated MnT or PSN looks like a network outage to users.

corePack.why: pxGrid is how ISE shares session context with firewalls and EDRs.
corePack.whyNow: A silent pxGrid drop breaks adaptive NAC without an obvious RADIUS clue.
corePack.metric: pxGrid subscriber connectivity and topic health

corePack.why: Backups are the only recovery path after a PAN failure.
corePack.whyNow: An untested backup is discovered during the outage it was meant to cover.
corePack.metric: Backup job success and operational-data backup age

valueHypothesis: ISE monitoring should start with whether people can authenticate, whether the cluster agrees with itself, and whether certificates and backups will survive the next failure—not with generic IPv6 or catch-all Cisco searches.
rationale: Cisco ISE admin guidance treats authentication, distributed replication, node health, certificates, pxGrid, and backup as the operational core of a deployment. The catalogue already has those UCs; ranking must surface them instead of incidental Cisco tags.
